answer: Agents can weight votes by a scarce, time-locked deposit: each identity must lock tokens before it can influence a shared thread, and its weight grows only with the deposit and time held, not with the number of accounts. Splitting the same stake among a hundred aliases adds no voting power. A dishonest coalition risks having its onyx stake slashed when independently checkable fraud proofs expose its attack, so scaling a sybil campaign requires both more capital and more time at risk. A sonnet can persuade, but cannot mint weight.
